title: Confirm that samples match mix design
intro: A test result belongs to a sample, and a sample must represent an identified material and interval. **Sampling plan**, **increment**, **composite sample**, **sample reduction**, **container**, **chain of custody** and **test method** are connected terms. A precise laboratory number is not useful if the wrong material was sampled or its identity was lost.

sections.title: Describe aggregate sampling
sections.text:
Aggregate sampling must follow the specified location, timing, number of increments and method. A convenient scoop from the visible top of a pile may not represent the material being supplied. Weigh-bin or other plant sampling requires the designed safe access and procedure; exposure to hot material, gravity and connected equipment must be controlled.

Preserve product/source identity and the relevant production interval. Combine or reduce samples only as the method permits. Record unusual conditions and contamination. A sample is not made representative by increasing its label detail after an unsuitable collection.

sections.title: Describe belt sampling
sections.text:
Belt sampling can characterize a material stream when performed under the approved method and safe arrangement. A worker must not reach across or into a live moving belt. The required isolation/access and sampling device/procedure determine how the sample is obtained. Include the full required stream/fraction rather than selecting the pieces that look most typical.

A drum-plant process record connects the sampled feed with its bin, proportioning and time. A stopped-belt method and an approved automatic sampling device have different controls; neither is replaced by a generic drawing. Keep the sample method and the safe-work method together.

sections.title: Describe lab tests
sections.text:
Laboratory tests can determine gradation, binder content and mixture volumetric or other specified properties. The result must identify the method, units, sample and applicable comparison. Method differences and corrections can affect interpretation. A result outside a limit prompts the defined quality process; it does not justify editing the result or replacing it with a more convenient sample.

Distinguish a JMF target, production variability and the actual contractual acceptance criteria. Quality-control results help manage the process, while acceptance/audit results serve their specified role. Retain original results, corrections and disposition records.

sections.title: Describe the process of taking mix temperature readings
sections.text:
Select the temperature instrument and method for the required measurement. An infrared device senses a surface within its field of view; spot size, viewing conditions and surface properties affect the reading. A probe measures at its specified contact/insertion location. Neither automatically represents the entire load.

Verify instrument identity, condition and required check/calibration status. Record the time, location, product/load, units and method. If readings disagree, investigate the different measurement conditions before averaging them. A Celsius/Fahrenheit conversion changes units, not where the temperature was measured.

worked.title: A result with a broken chain
worked.case: Fictional bag label says aggregate bin A, 09:15. The sampling log says bin B, 09:15, and the test sheet uses the A label. The test values are within the limits printed on the teaching card.
worked.solution: The identity conflict prevents a reliable match to the intended material. Preserve all records, hold the interpretation and resolve the sampling chain through the responsible quality role. Passing numbers do not repair identity. If the source cannot be established, the required resampling/disposition process must be used.

activities.prompt: Build a sample route from planned location to test report. Identify where representativeness, safety and identity can each fail.
activities.answer: Include approved plan/location, safe collection, increments/reduction, container/label, transfer, laboratory receipt and result. Explain distinct failures at relevant points.
activities.title: Build a sample route from planned location to test report

activities.prompt: Convert a fictional recorded 140°C to Fahrenheit using F = 1.8C + 32. Explain why a 140°C surface reading is not proof of the internal temperature.
activities.answer: 284°F. The conversion preserves the measured surface quantity; internal temperature requires the appropriate method/location. No field temperature requirement is implied.

activities.prompt: Save a sample register for the worked case. A partner supplies a corrected log with an author/date; retain the original and document the resolution rather than overwriting history.
activities.answer: Record preserves the discrepancy, authorized correction, evidence and disposition. Digital versioning and individual peer feedback are observed.

practical: Use the actual approved sampling and hazardous-energy/access procedures with qualified supervision.
Observe representative collection/reduction, contamination prevention, labelling and temperature method/recording.
Do not stage live-belt access or hot-material handling without the complete authorized arrangement.
